description: Compute sunrise, sunset and day length for any date and latitude using standard solar equations — no location lookup needed.

faqs.a: It uses the standard astronomical formulas: solar declination, the equation of time and the sunrise hour angle with a 90.833° zenith (accounts for refraction).
Yes — enter values beyond ±66.5° in summer/winter and it correctly reports polar day (24h daylight) or polar night (0h).
faqs.q: Does it handle polar day and night?

faqs.a: Add your longitude and UTC offset to convert solar times into local clock times.
faqs.q: How do I get clock times instead of just day length?

howto: Pick a date and enter your latitude (-90 to 90).
Optionally add longitude and your UTC offset for clock times.
Read sunrise, sunset, solar noon and total day length.
title: Daylight Hours Calculator
